mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.2% in the same month signals a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with weakening inflationary pressure, which increases uncertainty and reduces risk appetite, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% AND CPIAUCSL falls > -0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average +10% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month and a fall in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% in the same month signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressure and inflation risk, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in an expansionary regime.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > +0.5% AND UNRATE < 5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes in expansionary regimes at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for four consecutive quarters signals a broad-based demand shortfall, which depresses corporate earnings and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during all quarters where GDPC1 < 1% annualized for four consecutive quarters at 5% significance.
